reason: The cited evidence confirms that Al can form a protective Al₂O₃ scale (E3) and that Mn-rich oxides are non-protective (E1, E2, E4), but no cited passage provides direct support for the key premise that grain refinement accelerates selective Al oxidation or that the combination of higher Al and grain refinement yields a thinner, more adherent Al₂O₃ scale with lower mass gain.
premises: Increasing Al content promotes preferential Al₂O₃ formation in HEAs
Grain refinement accelerates selective oxidation of Al via increased grain-boundary density
A dense, continuous Al₂O₃ scale acts as a robust barrier limiting oxygen ingress and outward cation diffusion
In baseline coarse-grained, lower-Al HEAs, competing oxidation of mobile elements (e.g., Mn, Cr) produces non-protective mixed scales
The modified alloy will show lower mass gain and a thinner, more adherent Al₂O₃ scale than the baseline
